message.content:
Year 1600: in a world without coal hunger, river mills and animal teams shaped cities; guilds preserved craft, and wind-driven canals carried silk between ports, while scholars mapped the stars by lantern light, all before the forge would ever learn the word Year
Year 1750: the textile looms still clicked by hand, and philosophers debated steam in salons, yet no factory whistled; instead, botanical gardens grew into vertical towers where glass terraces harvested sunlight, and merchants sailed by compass and song, preserving a slow, luminous Year
Year 1850: without smokestacks, cities climbed as stacked marketplaces of copper and reed, powered by trained wind and tidal springs; libraries became living forests of paper vines, and children learned the language of clouds, believing the century a gentle Year
Year 1950: radio waves still crossed oceans, but no electric grid hummed; instead, solar mosaics and wind-lilies powered lamps, while flying carpets of woven silk carried mail above terraced rice fields, making the mid-century feel like a floating Year
Year 2050: the world’s gardens reached the moon in slow seedships, guided by bioluminescent bees and ancient star maps; humanity spoke in pollen-coded dreams, tended the oceans with coral choirs, and called its endless, unpolluted future Year
